To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ca2+, Mg2+ and F- stimulate IP4 accumulation in parathyroid glands.
inositol phosphates, especially IP3, play a role in Ca2+ signaling and that the Ca2+-dependent increase in IP3 is not mediated through the Ca2+ receptor.
Ca2+ and F- increase IP3 and IP4 in parathormone-secreting bovine parathyroids cells, and Mg2+ increases IP4 in these cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the parathyroid gland responds to the extracellular calcium (Ca2+) concentration.
the role of calcium in regulating parathyroid hormone secretion and the mechanisms of action of parathyroid hormone in regulating the metabolism of bone and kidney.
the role of calcium and magnesium in the regulation of the parathyroid gland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IP4 is not a likely candidate as a Ca2+ mobilizing messenger in parathyroid hormone (PTH) release.
IP4 may be involved in the late phase of the Ca2+ response to high extracelluar calcium concentrations.
the IP4 is a mediator of the increase in cytosol Ca2+.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IP3, IP4, and IP6 are all involved in the regulation of Ca2+ homeostasis.
IP3 is the primary messenger in parathyroid gland cells for Ca2+ signaling.
Ca2+ is a very effective activator of the parathyroid cell phosphoinositide system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IP4 can be generated in parathyroid gland cells, which could potentially modulate the effects of high extrellular Ca2+ on parathyroid hormone secretion.

IP4 is not a mediator of the Ca2+ signal produced by extracellular Ca2+, but that IP4 may be involved in the sustained increase in Ca2+ produced through the action of high extracellular Mg2+ concentrations.
